headline: Sensex rallies 905 points; Reliance and Jio report today as tech rout hits Asia

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Friday, the thirtieth of October, and here is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, Dalal Street had its best day in a while on Thursday. The Sensex jumped 905 points after the American central bank held rates and oil eased. But this morning a sharp sell-off in technology shares on Wall Street is spilling into Asia, so the open here is muted.

Second, it is a big results day. Reliance Industries and Jio Platforms both report today, Jio for the first time as a listed company.

And third, the finance ministry estimates the economy grew around 7.35 percent in the September quarter, but it is now calling price stability the top priority for the rest of the year, with oil still above 115 dollars a barrel.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Markets opened lower on Thursday but turned around and closed at the day's high. The Sensex ended 905 points up at 74,151. The Nifty gained 238 points to close at 22,936. That added nearly five lakh crore rupees to investors' wealth. Realty was the best sector, with consumer goods close behind. The Adani group rallied up to 6 percent after strong numbers from Adani Enterprises and Adani Ports, and Kotak Mahindra Bank hit a record high, up nearly 30 percent since April.

Now to the money flows. Foreign institutional investors snapped a two-day buying streak and sold shares worth about 943 crore rupees. Domestic institutions bought about 1,924 crore rupees, their second straight day of buying.

There is a note of caution under the surface. The Economic Times says the ratio of rising to falling shares has hit a seven-month low, with midcap and smallcap indices down this month. And Mint points out that the Sensex and Nifty are still down around 12 to 13 percent this year.

This morning, the Sensex is roughly flat around 74,200 and the Nifty is just above 22,950. Trent is up about 6 percent after its results, and Equitas Small Finance Bank is down about 11 percent.

The levels to watch: Moneycontrol's analysts say the Nifty needs to hold 22,800 to push on towards 23,000 to 23,200, where the fifty-day average sits near 23,164. A break below 22,800 could bring 22,650 and then 22,400 into view.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
In the primary market, the Bombay Coated and Special Steels issue is open. It is a fresh issue of about 183 crore rupees and runs until the second of November. Wiscon Industries' small-company issue got through on its final day, helped by institutional buyers. Allotment is due today, and the shares list on the third of November.

On the deals side, the promoter of Sagility is selling about a 12 percent stake through a block deal worth around 2,377 crore rupees. Moneycontrol's sources put the price near 42 rupees 45 paise, a discount of about 5 percent to Thursday's close.

And a report from Grant Thornton Bharat says pharma and healthcare deal volumes rose 23 percent in the July to September quarter, to 87 deals worth 4.3 billion dollars.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to the September quarter results, and a clear theme. As a Moneycontrol column put it, commodity companies have done well on higher prices, while those same costs are hurting consumer businesses.

Starting with commodities. Coal India's profit jumped 57 percent to 6,547 crore rupees, from 4,167 crore a year ago, on revenue of about 44,179 crore. On the other side, Ambuja Cements' profit slumped 90 percent to 236 crore rupees, as fuel and freight costs squeezed margins and revenue stayed flat.

In consumer and retail, Trent's profit rose 25 percent to 468 crore rupees, and revenue grew 22 percent to 5,873 crore. It opened 29 new stores, and Bahram Vakil takes over as chairman as Noel Tata retires. Godrej Consumer's profit rose 14 percent, but the company says it is weighing price hikes on soaps and liquid detergents as costs climb.

In aviation, IndiGo swung to a loss of 1,879 crore rupees. Revenue rose 26 percent to about 23,364 crore, but fuel costs surged more than 67 percent. The airline plans to raise fares and trim flights. Even so, Jefferies, Nomura and HSBC kept their buy ratings, and the shares rose about 2 percent.

In finance, Motilal Oswal Financial Services tripled its profit to 1,081 crore rupees. SBI Mutual Fund's average assets rose 10 percent to 13.1 lakh crore rupees. And Tata Capital rallied over 5 percent after its numbers.

A few more. Suzlon's profit rose just 1.3 percent, though revenue grew 26 percent on higher turbine deliveries. Brigade's profit rose 29 percent to 219 crore. Meesho's loss narrowed to about 132 crore rupees, from 411 crore. And in technology, eClerx fell 13 percent despite an 18 percent rise in revenue, while Birlasoft rallied 11 percent.

Today, all eyes are on Reliance. Business Standard says brokerages expect its revenue to grow 22 to 30 percent from a year ago.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
To the economy. The finance ministry's monthly review estimates growth of about 7.35 percent in the September quarter, after 7.8 percent in the June quarter. It credits factory output, tax collections, power use, port traffic and car sales. But it lists high crude prices, food inflation, a weak rupee and high American bond yields as risks, and says price stability is the priority for the rest of the year.

The International Monetary Fund says India remains an engine of world growth, with its forecast at 7 percent for this financial year and next. It says the risks from a Super El Nino have not yet shown up, and it will look again in January. The agricultural economist Ashok Gulati is more worried. He told Moneycontrol farm growth could turn negative this year, and fertiliser subsidies could reach 3 lakh crore rupees.

On the brighter side, services grew widely in August. Seventeen of nineteen segments expanded, led by retail trade, up nearly 20 percent.

Now to the rupee and rates. The rupee closed three paise stronger at 95.25 to the dollar. Reuters, writing in Business Standard, says the ten-year bond yield is near its highest since 2022, with traders betting on another Reserve Bank rate hike in December, possibly by half a percentage point. And the rating agency Icra says that if crude stays between 105 and 115 dollars, oil companies could lose over 64,000 crore rupees on petrol and diesel this year.

One more for the tax watchers. The debate on capital gains tax is heating up. The industry body PHDCCI has asked the finance ministry to abolish long-term capital gains tax on shares. Jefferies says the options before the government range from special treatment for foreign investors to a cut for everyone. Boston Consulting Group's India chairman, Janmejaya Sinha, calls a cut a short-term fix, and says India must tackle its current account deficit.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, the American Federal Reserve held its rate range at 3.75 to 4 percent. Its chair, Kevin Warsh, said fighting inflation comes first, and announced fewer rate meetings from 2027. American growth also came in strong, at 3.4 percent for the quarter, ahead of forecasts.

But Wall Street had a rough night. Alphabet fell about 10 percent after weak search and advertising sales, its biggest-ever loss of market value. Intel tumbled on a weak outlook, and Amazon slipped after hours on a revenue miss. Worries about heavy spending on artificial intelligence are back, and Nasdaq futures are down around 2 percent. In Korea, Samsung reported a record profit on demand for memory chips.

Oil is back up. Brent crude rose to about 115.7 dollars a barrel after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, reversing Thursday's dip on hopes of talks between America and Iran. Gold is steady near 4,000 dollars an ounce, heading for a second monthly loss.

And in crypto, Binance has frozen about 2.5 billion dollars of assets while it looks into a suspected hack that could be the largest ever. Bitcoin slipped below 79,000 dollars.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script:
An update on the Jio IPO you're following. In its second session, Jio rose as much as 5 percent, taking it about 33 percent above the issue price, with a market value near 13.7 lakh crore rupees. It reports its first results as a listed company today.

And on the India-US trade deal, Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that the agreement protects every sensitive Indian interest, including farmers, and that people will celebrate once the details are out.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money. If you trade on margin, take note. The National Stock Exchange's inspections found brokers giving margin trading funding against shares that are not eligible, mishandling client funds and falling short on cybersecurity. It is worth checking your broker's statements.

For employers, the government has extended the amnesty scheme under the Employees' State Insurance Act by three months, to the thirty-first of December. It covers court cases filed up to the thirty-first of March 2025.

The provident fund body, EPFO, is drafting rules to put up to 3 percent of its fresh inflows each year into startup and alternative investment funds. Farmers will get the twenty-fourth instalment of PM-KISAN, worth about 19,000 crore rupees, during the Prime Minister's Gujarat visit. And for gold buyers, gold on the domestic commodity exchange was around 1,43,600 rupees for ten grams on Thursday.

That's the brief. Today, watch whether the Nifty can hold 22,800 after the overnight tech sell-off, and keep an eye on oil after the attacks on Saudi Arabia. And Reliance and Jio report their numbers later today. Have a good Friday, and a good weekend.
